info.title: Analyze open PRs for overlap and gaps (@explore subagent)

parts.text:
You are analyzing open pull requests on the GitHub repo `alehar9320/agentic-odi` to find opportunities for improvement, overlap, duplication, and risk. Read-only analysis; do NOT write files or comment on GitHub.

Use the `gh` CLI (already authenticated). Start with:
- `gh pr list --state open --limit 60 --json number,title,author,headRefName,createdAt,updatedAt,isDraft,additions,deletions,changedFiles,body,url`
- `gh pr view <N> --json ...` for details, plus `gh pr diff <N> --name-only` and `gh pr diff <N>` (pipe to a file in /tmp if large).
- `gh pr checks <N>` to see CI status.
- Also look at the branches: `gh api repos/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branches` or `git log origin/<branch>` since the repo is cloned at /home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi with `origin` remote. You can run `git log --oneline origin/<branch> -15` and `git diff --stat origin/main...origin/<branch>` to see each PR's real delta without checking out.
- `gh issue list --state all --limit 50` for existing issues.

The open PRs I already know about are roughly:
#76 feat(studio): make the desktop app update itself
#70 feat(evidence): add signals and evidence storage delegation with external links
#66 feat(studio): elevate mobile UX with 20 touch-first micro-improvements
#65 feat: add on-device llm fallback and model router
#64 feat: capture V2MOM artifacts in domain context and conversational experience
#63 refactor(studio): improve UX copy and visual clarity across studio components
#62 feat: add foundation for cloud agent work scheduling
Also check for any others I may have missed, and for closed-but-recently-merged PRs that reveal direction of travel.

For EACH open PR, report:
- What it actually changes (files, new modules, new domain entities, new tools, new endpoints, new UI surfaces) — read the diff, don't trust the body.
- Whether it is a real implementation or a "mock foundation" / stub (several say "mock foundation" or are machine-generated by Jules).
- CI status (passing/failing/pending).
- Overlap/conflict risk with `origin/main` and with other open PRs (e.g. do #63, #66, #65, #64 all rewrite the same studio components? do #70 and #62 both touch the same core models?).
- What is left un-done or un-specified in that PR (acceptance criteria that a reviewer would check).

Then report:
- Which open PRs are BLOCKING or would conflict with each other (list the conflict matrix).
- Which PRs are "mock only" and therefore need a follow-up spec to become real.
- Gaps that NO open PR addresses (this is critical — I need to find opportunities that are not already claimed by a PR).
- The repo's CI/release/branch-protection state and any signs of churn (e.g. very large diffs, auto-generated PRs, release-please flow).

Be concrete: cite PR numbers, file paths, and line numbers. Do not write any files.
I'll start by gathering the PR list and repo state.

[{"additions":3431,"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjUzOTA0MzA=","is_bot":false,"login":"alehar9320","name":"Alexander"},"body":"## Why

An installed Living Studio could never update itself. The Tauri app was pinned at `0.1.0` while releases are cut at `0.11.0`, `Tauri Release` had never run (release-please publishes through the API, which never emits a `push: tags` event), no release carried a `latest.json`, and the only update affordance was a button buried in Settings that installed without asking and never relaunched.

This makes self-update real end to end.

## What a person experiences

- Four seconds after launch — never competing with first paint — the app checks quietly. It re-checks every six hours and when the window returns to the foreground after that long.
- A found update downloads in the background. One bar above the conversation shows progress; it never blocks, never takes focus, and can be dismissed.
- macOS and Linux stage the update as soon as its signature verifies, so it applies on the next ordinary launch even if nobody clicks anything. **Restart now** applies it immediately. Windows needs the app to exit for NSIS, so it offers **Update & restart**.
- **Settings → Software update** shows the running version, a plain-language status, the release notes, **Check now**, **Skip this version**, and the auto-check toggle. Check failures stay here instead of interrupting the conversation.
- The top bar shows the running version and quietly becomes **Update ready** when a restart will finish the job; both open the update settings.
- In the browser and in `tauri dev`, the section says honestly that in-app updates live in the installed desktop app.

## Architecture

```
apps/studio/src/updater/
  types.ts        domain vocabulary
  machine.ts      pure reducer + selectors (no I/O, no timers, no React)
  service.ts      schedule → check → download → install → relaunch, injected transport/storage/clock
  transport.ts    the only module that imports Tauri plugins
  platform.ts     macOS/Linux stage silently; Windows binds install to the explicit restart
  UpdateProvider.tsx  one service per app, shared via useSyncExternalStore
  UpdateBanner.tsx    the quiet bar
  UpdateSettings.tsx  the Settings section
```

Every surface derives from one snapshot, so the bar, the sidebar, and Settings cannot disagree. Background-check failures are silent by selector, not by convention.

`tauri-plugin-process` is registered with `process:default` for the in-place relaunch. The branch is rebased onto the one-room shell (`StudioBar`), so the indicator lives in the top bar.

## Release pipeline

- `release-please` now bumps `apps/studio/package.json`, `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, and `apps/studio/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` from `extra-files`; without this the installed version can never move.
- `Tauri Release` and `release` also trigger on `release: published`, which is the event release-please actually produces. `push: tags` stays for hand-cut tags.
- A new `verify` job fails the release if `latest.json` does not advertise the tag's version and carry signed artifacts for Linux, Windows, and both macOS architectures.
- The desktop version is synced to the current `0.12.0` so local builds match the manifest.

## Verification

- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test -- --run` (**267 tests**), `npm run build`.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo check`.
- **Real end-to-end proof**, not a mock: `scripts/verify-desktop-update.sh` builds two signed AppImages with a throwaway key, serves a local `latest.json`, runs 0.1.0, and watches it replace its own file:

```
OK: the running 0.1.0 replaced its own AppImage with 0.2.0
OK: the updated app reports no update and downloads nothing
```

  The installed file's sha256 equals the 0.2.0 build's, and the second run hit `/latest.json` without requesting the bundle — so the updater checked, downloaded, verified the signature, installed, and then correctly reported itself current.

## Notes

- The relaunch itself is covered by unit tests and is the canonical `@tauri-apps/plugin-process` `relaunch()` call; the E2E cannot click a button in a headless environment.
- Linux self-update applies to AppImage installs. A `.deb` install surfaces a clear error instead of silently doing nothing.
- This PR does not publish a release. The first release built after merge should be the first one that ships a working `latest.json`; the new `verify` job makes a failure loud.
- Design and plan: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-studio-auto-update-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-studio-auto-update.md`.

This pull request introduces **20 touch-first micro-improvements** to the Living Studio client frontend (`apps/studio`), turning it into a world-class mobile-friendly experience.

#### 20 Cataloged & Implemented Micro-Improvements:
1. **Viewport Optimization**: Added `viewport-fit=cover`, maximum-scale, and user-scalable constraints to `index.html`.
2. **Safe-Area Insets**: Standardized CSS custom variables (`env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`, `env(safe-area-inset-top)`) for notch and swipe-indicator padding.
3. **Touch Ergonomics (44px Rule)**: Enforced `min-height: 44px` across all interactive buttons, text inputs, selects, and checkboxes.
4. **Mobile Slide-Over Copilot Drawer**: Transformed `ChatCopilot` on mobile into a smooth bottom sheet with semi-transparent backdrop overlay.
5. **Floating Action Button (FAB)**: Added persistent `💬 AI Copilot` FAB on mobile screens for immediate assistant access.
6. **Horizontally Scrollable Tab Navigation**: Transformed `CanvasTabs` with swipeable scrollable tab list and hidden scrollbars.
7. **Shortened Mobile Tab Labels**: Added mobile-only compact tab labels (`🌟 Landscape`, `🗺️ Job Map`, `⚡ Impact`, etc.).
8. **Keyboard & Touch Accessibility**: Added arrow key navigation (`ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight`) and explicit ARIA `tablist`/`tab` roles.
9. **Engagement Level Quick Switcher**: Added `L0`/`L1`/`L2` toggle pill buttons directly in `StudioHeader` for rapid state switching on touch devices.
10. **Collapsible Settings Panel**: Set `SettingsPanel` default state to collapsed on initial render so key canvas content displays immediately on mobile.
11. **Unified Outcome Card Actions**: Integrated action buttons (`🔍 Trace`, `⚡ Simulate`, `💬 Ask AI`) inside the outcome card container.
12. **Simulate Navigation Workflow**: Wiring `⚡ Simulate` button on `OutcomeCard` to automatically activate the WYSIWYG Impact tab.
13. **Fluid Metrics Grid**: Adapted metrics grids to 1-column layout on small phone screens (< 480px) and 3-column on tablet/desktop.
14. **Stacked Form Comparison Grids**: Stacked `BEFORE` and `AFTER` impact comparison cards vertically on mobile viewports.
15. **Touch Target Dismiss Buttons**: Updated `Toasts` notifications with 44px × 44px touch targets for effortless thumb dismissal.
16. **Text Input Zoom Prevention**: Set standard font size to `0.95rem` / `15px` on inputs to prevent unwanted iOS Safari automatic zoom-on-focus.
17. **Tap Highlight Disabling**: Applied `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent` globally for native app touch feel.
18. **Mobile Quick Prompt Pills**: Formatted suggested intent pills in a horizontally scrolling strip above chat input.
19. **Smooth Auto-Scroll Guard**: Ensured chat log smoothly scrolls to bottom on new streaming tokens with fallback for test environments.
20. **Accessibility & High Contrast**: Boosted contrast ratios on status pills, text colors, and focus visible outlines (`:focus-visible`).

#### Verification & Testing
- **Vitest Unit Tests**: Added `MobileUX.test.tsx` testing header controls, canvas tabs, chat drawer FAB, outcome cards, and settings toggles (29 total tests passing).
- **TypeScript & Build**: Clean `tsc -b` typecheck, `vite build`, and zero `eslint` warnings.
- **Python Test Suite**: All 546 pytest suite tests pass.
- **Playwright Verification**: Generated video and screenshots confirming mobile viewport rendering.

parts.text:
Now the mechanism is clear. The Jules commits are **cumulative** — each subsequent commit in the branch re-writes the whole tree. The "deleting" commits are Jules commits where a *later* commit in the same branch deletes files.

E.g. for #63: `040a65a5` shows theme.css 374 added / 2911 deleted. That means the *previous* commit in the branch had a big theme.css, and this commit replaced it with a small one. But the base 624b6857's theme.css must be even bigger.

Wait, I need to check the actual net effect. Let me check theme.css size at main vs branch head.

Actually the important thing for the analysis: the NET diff of each PR against main shows deletions of key feature files. Let me confirm concretely: does `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` exist in origin/main and NOT in the PR head?

Yes, merge-base 624b6857 has it. Let me check the head of each branch.

So the net effect of merging #63, #66, #65, #70, #64, #62 into main would DELETE:
- `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` (from #55 "conversational rich surfaces")
- `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx`
- `apps/studio/src/ui/protocol.ts`
- `apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.tsx` + `steps.tsx` + `onboarding.css` (from #69 "first-run wizard")
- `apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx` (from #58)
- `apps/studio/src/components/setup/SetupConversation.tsx` (from #43)
- `apps/studio/src/App.test.tsx`
- `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_ui_spec.py`
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-20-storage-provider-sync.md` (from #42)

This is a catastrophic regression: merging any of these PRs reverts 4-5 recently merged features.

Let me verify this concretely with file existence checks on branch heads.

Also, why does CI pass on #66/#65/#63 but their trees are missing files? Because the deletions came with the tree state... Hmm, if `FirstRunWizard.tsx` is deleted but `StudioContext.tsx` still imports it, the typecheck would fail. Unless... the StudioContext.tsx is also reverted to the pre-#69 version, in which case the whole tree is self-consistent (an old snapshot of the studio frontend).

Yes! That's it: **Jules committed an old snapshot of the entire studio frontend**, reverting the studio app to a pre-#43/#55/#58/#69 state. So it's self-consistent and CI passes, but it silently reverts ~4 merged features worth thousands of lines.

Let me verify: check StudioContext.tsx at branch head vs main.

Let me now do a systematic check of what feature-reverting is in each branch head.
Now the mechanism is clear: the Jules branches commit a **stale snapshot of the whole studio frontend**. Let me verify the net reverts.

So the Jules PRs add back components (`StudioHeader.tsx`, `CanvasTabs.tsx`, `ChatCopilot.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx`) that no longer exist in main — they are **orphaned duplicates** of main's new `StudioBar` / `ChatStage` / `WorkbenchRail`. Provides multi-tier routing (Rule-based, On-Device Local LLM, Remote Smart LLM)
with automatic fallback and user settings support.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable
from enum import Enum

from agentic_odi_core.steve_jobs import generate_steve_jobs_response


class ModelTier(str, Enum):
    """Model execution tiers."""

    RULE_BASED = "rule_based"  # Tier 0: On-device instant rule-based engine (Steve Jobs pass)
    ON_DEVICE_LLM = "on_device_llm"  # Tier 1: On-device / local GGUF / tiny model engine
    REMOTE_LLM = "remote_llm"  # Tier 2: Remote / smart cloud LLM backend


class RoutingMode(str, Enum):
    """Routing modes for model selection."""

    AUTO = "auto"  # Auto-select smartest available tier, transparent fallback
    FORCE_RULE_BASED = "rule_based"  # Force Tier 0
    FORCE_ON_DEVICE = "on_device"  # Force Tier 1
    FORCE_REMOTE = "remote"  # Force Tier 2


class OnDeviceLLMEngine:
    """Minimal lightweight on-device LLM engine wrapper / mock interface."""

    def __init__(self, model_name: str = "on-device-tiny-llm") -> None:
        self.model_name = model_name

    def is_available(self) -> bool:
        """Check if on-device model files/runtime are ready."""
        return True

    async def generate_stream(self, prompt: str) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
        """Generate response chunks from on-device model."""
        response = generate_steve_jobs_response(prompt)
        words = response.split(" ")
        for i, word in enumerate(words):
            chunk = word if i == 0 else " " + word
            yield chunk
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)


class ModelRouter:

        if self.mode == RoutingMode.FORCE_RULE_BASED:

        if self.mode == RoutingMode.FORCE_ON_DEVICE:

        if self.mode == RoutingMode.FORCE_REMOTE:

        if self.on_device_engine.is_available():

        return ModelTier.RULE_BASED

=== ci.yml (main) ===
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy
        run: uv run mypy apps packages

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest
        run: |
          uv run pytest \
            --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
            --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
            --cov=agentic_odi_core \
            --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
            --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API
        run: |
          AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND=mcp uv run python -m agentic_odi_studio_api.main > /tmp/sidecar.log 2>&1 &
          SIDECAR_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/health/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&
              curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: scripts/dev.py brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

  website:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Pytest (website)
        run: uv run --directory website pytest tests/

      - name: Build site (rsync)
        run: |
          mkdir -p _site
          rsync -av website/ _site/ --exclude='tests/' --exclude='tools/'

  studio:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test -- --run

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Verify generated API types are up to date
        run: |
          npm run gen:api-types
          git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts

  tauri-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio/src-tauri
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo check
        run: cargo check

  tauri-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: apps/studio

      # Dependabot PRs cannot read repository secrets, so the signing key is
      # empty there. Export it only when present and disable updater artifacts
      # otherwise; passing an empty key makes the bundler try (and fail) to
      # decode it.
      - name: Build desktop bundle
        working-directory: apps/studio
        env:
          SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$SIGNING_KEY"
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="$SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD"
            npm run tauri -- build
          else
            echo "No TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY provided — building without signed updater artifacts."
            npm run tauri -- build --config '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'
          fi

      - name: Upload desktop bundles
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: tauri-bundles-linux
          if-no-files-found: warn
          path: |
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/*.deb
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage.sig

  ci-green:
    name: CI green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke, website, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify all required jobs succeeded
        run: |
          results='${{ join(needs.*.result, ' ') }}'
          echo "Job results: $results"
          for result in $results; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::A required job did not succeed ($results)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "OK: all required jobs succeeded"

 name: Tauri Release
 
+# release-please creates the GitHub release through the API, which does not
+# emit a `push` event for the tag. Listening for the published release is what
+# actually starts the desktop build (and therefore publishes latest.json, which
+# the in-app updater depends on). `push` stays for tags created by hand.

=== ci.yml (main) ===
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy
        run: uv run mypy apps packages

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest
        run: |
          uv run pytest \
            --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
            --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
            --cov=agentic_odi_core \
            --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
            --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API
        run: |
          AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND=mcp uv run python -m agentic_odi_studio_api.main > /tmp/sidecar.log 2>&1 &
          SIDECAR_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/health/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&
              curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: scripts/dev.py brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

  website:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Pytest (website)
        run: uv run --directory website pytest tests/

      - name: Build site (rsync)
        run: |
          mkdir -p _site
          rsync -av website/ _site/ --exclude='tests/' --exclude='tools/'

  studio:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test -- --run

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Verify generated API types are up to date
        run: |
          npm run gen:api-types
          git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts

  tauri-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio/src-tauri
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo check
        run: cargo check

  tauri-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: apps/studio

      # Dependabot PRs cannot read repository secrets, so the signing key is
      # empty there. Export it only when present and disable updater artifacts
      # otherwise; passing an empty key makes the bundler try (and fail) to
      # decode it.
      - name: Build desktop bundle
        working-directory: apps/studio
        env:
          SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$SIGNING_KEY"
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="$SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD"
            npm run tauri -- build
          else
            echo "No TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY provided — building without signed updater artifacts."
            npm run tauri -- build --config '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'
          fi

      - name: Upload desktop bundles
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: tauri-bundles-linux
          if-no-files-found: warn
          path: |
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/*.deb
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage.sig

  ci-green:
    name: CI green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke, website, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify all required jobs succeeded
        run: |
          results='${{ join(needs.*.result, ' ') }}'
          echo "Job results: $results"
          for result in $results; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::A required job did not succeed ($results)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "OK: all required jobs succeeded"

for b in $(git branch -r | grep -v 'origin/main\|origin/master\|origin/HEAD\|origin/release-please' | sed 's/ *origin\///'); do
  n=$(git rev-list --count origin/main..origin/$b 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$n" != "0" ] && [ -n "$n" ]; then
    echo "--- $b ($n commits ahead of main) ---"
    git log --oneline origin/main..origin/$b 2>/dev/null | head -6
  fi
done

=== docs/roadmap.md ===
# Roadmap & Next Steps

As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include:

- [x] **External MCP client connector**: Pluggable connectors package with an
  HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests.
- [x] **Conversational rich surfaces**: the studio agent composes validated
  cards inline from a closed, client-owned catalog instead of describing them
  in prose.
- [x] **Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts**: Turn connector records into
  jobs, outcomes, or evidence without mixing connector plumbing into the ODI
  store.
- [x] **First-run wizard**: A skippable, resumable four-step tour with inline
  connection repair, ending in the chosen surface or a handoff to the context
  conversation — isolated in `apps/studio/src/onboarding/` behind the
  `firstRunWizard` flag.
- [x] **Additional connector kinds**: REST/webhooks and similar integrations
  implementing the same `Connector` protocol.
- [x] **ODI Schema Definition**: Define standardized Pydantic models for *Jobs*,
  *Steps*, and *Outcomes*.
- [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: Extend `apps/cli` so the ODI dataset can be
  created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current
  MCP path.
- [x] **Context Tooling**: Replace the dummy `greet` tool with capabilities like
  `get_job_map(job_id)`, `get_outcomes(job_id)`, `get_step(step_id)`,
  `get_outcome(outcome_id)`, or `evaluate_outcome(statement)`.
- [x] **Data Persistence Layer**: Connect the FastMCP server to a lightweight
  SQLite repository containing actual user research data.
- [x] **Agentic Integration**: Hook the CLI chat up to an LLM (via the
  `openai` package) so the LLM can *discover* the ODI tools and intelligently
  request customer insights when ideating features.

=== docs/roadmap.md ===
# Roadmap & Next Steps

As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include:

- [x] **External MCP client connector**: Pluggable connectors package with an
  HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests.
- [x] **Conversational rich surfaces**: the studio agent composes validated
  cards inline from a closed, client-owned catalog instead of describing them
  in prose.
- [x] **Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts**: Turn connector records into
  jobs, outcomes, or evidence without mixing connector plumbing into the ODI
  store.
- [x] **First-run wizard**: A skippable, resumable four-step tour with inline
  connection repair, ending in the chosen surface or a handoff to the context
  conversation — isolated in `apps/studio/src/onboarding/` behind the
  `firstRunWizard` flag.
- [x] **Additional connector kinds**: REST/webhooks and similar integrations
  implementing the same `Connector` protocol.
- [x] **ODI Schema Definition**: Define standardized Pydantic models for *Jobs*,
  *Steps*, and *Outcomes*.
- [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: Extend `apps/cli` so the ODI dataset can be
  created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current
  MCP path.
- [x] **Context Tooling**: Replace the dummy `greet` tool with capabilities like
  `get_job_map(job_id)`, `get_outcomes(job_id)`, `get_step(step_id)`,
  `get_outcome(outcome_id)`, or `evaluate_outcome(statement)`.
- [x] **Data Persistence Layer**: Connect the FastMCP server to a lightweight
  SQLite repository containing actual user research data.
- [x] **Agentic Integration**: Hook the CLI chat up to an LLM (via the
  `openai` package) so the LLM can *discover* the ODI tools and intelligently
  request customer insights when ideating features.

echo "=== docs/roadmap.md ==="
git show origin/main:docs/roadmap.md
echo
echo "=== abandoned / unmerged branches: commits not in main ==="
for b in $(git branch -r | grep -v 'origin/main\|origin/master\|origin/HEAD\|origin/release-please' | sed 's/ *origin\///'); do
  n=$(git rev-list --count origin/main..origin/$b 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$n" != "0" ] && [ -n "$n" ]; then
    echo "--- $b ($n commits ahead of main) ---"
    git log --oneline origin/main..origin/$b 2>/dev/null | head -6
  fi
done

# Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend

To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a
local LLM backend that:

- Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example,
  `/v1/chat/completions`), and
- Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**.

A simple fully local option is
[`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run
a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server.

## 1. Install a local LLM server

Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for
platform-specific build notes):

```bash
pip install llama-cpp-python
```

## 2. Download a small tools-capable model

Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a
7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g.
`C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`.

## 3. Start the OpenAI-compatible server

Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default
used by the Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat:

```bash
python -m llama_cpp.server \
  --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \
  --model_alias local-tools-model \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \
  --chat_format openai
```

This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`.

## 4. Configure the Studio

The Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat read the following environment
variables (with sensible defaults):

| Variable | Default |
|---|---|
| `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` |

You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Living Studio's
**Settings** panel.

## 5. Verify tool-calling against the MCP server

- (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable:

  ```bash
  curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models
  ```

  If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before
  debugging the MCP client/server.

- Start the MCP server and Studio (via `python scripts/dev.py` or one of the
  [run modes](living-studio.md)).
- In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for
  example: *"Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI
  repository."*
- You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for
  example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI
  guidance, confirming the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work
  together.
- If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI shows a clear error
  banner indicating the configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with
  details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps
  above to fix your local LLM setup.

## 6. On-Device LLM & Fallback Routing

Agentic ODI includes a built-in multi-tier **Model Router** (`agentic_odi_core.router`) that ensures an instant, delightful on-device fallback experience:

- **Tier 0 (`rule_based`)**: Instant zero-latency rule-based engine formatted with Steve Jobs clarity for stage guidelines, opportunity score calculations, and impact simulations.
- **Tier 1 (`on_device_llm`)**: Local on-device LLM runner for standalone offline experience.
- **Tier 2 (`remote_llm`)**: Smartest remote or local OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint.

In default **`auto`** mode, the system automatically routes requests to the smartest available tier, falling back silently and instantly when remote models are unreachable. Advanced users can override the routing mode via Settings or configuration files (`auto`, `rule_based`, `on_device`, `remote`).

=== .agents/rules/agent_instructions.md (domain guardrails) ===
# Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails

This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.

> **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.

---

## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails

This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.

### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?

ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.

ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.

---

### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done

- A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
- A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
- **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
- ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.

---

### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes

- **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
- Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
- **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):

  > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`

  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.

- **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.

---

### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)

- All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
  1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
  2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
  3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
  4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
  5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
  6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
  7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
  8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs

- **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
- ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.

---

### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)

- Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
  - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
  - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?

- **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):

  ```
  Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
  ```

- **Interpretation**:
  - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
  - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
  - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.

- **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.

---

### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation

- ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
- Segments can be:
  - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
  - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
  - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value

- **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.

---

### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy

Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:

| Strategy | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
| **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
| **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |

- **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.

---

### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent

These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:

| DO | DON'T |
|---|---|
| Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
| Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
| Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
| Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
| Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
| Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
| Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |

---

## 🛠 Technology Stack & Tools
- **Language**: Python 3.10+
- **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)
- **ASGI Server**: `uvicorn`
- **HTTP Client**: `httpx`
- **UI / Chat Client**: React + Vite (`apps/studio`), FastAPI sidecar (`apps/studio-api`)
- **LLM Client**: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible, used with Ollama locally)
- **Concurrency**: `asyncio`
- **Data Modeling / Validation**: `pydantic`

---

## 📄 README Maintenance Guardrail

`README.md` is the **primary human-facing entry point** for this project: a short,
high-level front door aimed at both users and developers. Detailed material lives
in `docs/` and is linked from the README. The agent MUST keep both current at all
times.

### When to update

Update the relevant file whenever any of the following change:

| Change type | Where to update |
|---|---|
| New or removed Python file / package | `README.md` **Code Overview** |
| New dependency added (`pip install ...`) | `README.md` **Quick Start → Prerequisites** |
| New way to run the project | `README.md` **Quick Start** and `docs/living-studio.md` |
| New MCP tool or capability | `README.md` **Code Overview** / relevant doc |
| New CLI command or flag | `docs/cli.md` |
| New connector kind | `docs/connectors.md` |
| New workflow or agent instruction | `docs/living-studio.md` |
| Deployment URL or cloud setup changes | `docs/deployment.md` |
| Roadmap item completed or added | `docs/roadmap.md` |
| Test layout or coverage changes | `docs/development.md` |

### Rules

- ✅ **Update docs in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
- ✅ **Keep README short**: it stays a high-level orientation page. Push detail into `docs/` and link to it rather than growing the README.
- ✅ **Keep the Quick Start accurate**: always reflect `uv run python scripts/dev.py` as the recommended launch command.
- ✅ **Keep Prerequisites up to date**: add any new `pip install` dependency immediately.
- ✅ **Mark Roadmap items `[x]` when completed** — do not leave stale unchecked items.
- ❌ **Never leave the README or `docs/` in a stale state** where documented commands or files no longer match the codebase.

---

## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails

### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
- **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
- **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
  - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
  - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
- **Tool Creation**: 
  - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
  - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
  - **Contract Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` (`ToolName`, `TOOL_SPECS`) and the `get_capabilities` return string. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` enforces the surface.

### 2. Async / Client Practices
- Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
- Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.

### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
- Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
- When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.

### 4. General Philosophy
- **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
- **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
- **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `packages/connectors` workspace package. New kinds implement `agentic_odi_connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
- **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.

### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
- **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
- **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
- **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `packages/connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
- **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
- **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
- **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
- **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.

- ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
- Segments can be:
  - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
  - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
  - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value

- **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.

---

### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy

Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:

| Strategy | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
| **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
| **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |

- **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.

---

### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent

These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:

| DO | DON'T |
|---|---|
| Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
| Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
| Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
| Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
| Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
| Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
| Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |

---

## 🛠 Technology Stack & Tools
- **Language**: Python 3.10+
- **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)
- **ASGI Server**: `uvicorn`
- **HTTP Client**: `httpx`
- **UI / Chat Client**: React + Vite (`apps/studio`), FastAPI sidecar (`apps/studio-api`)
- **LLM Client**: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible, used with Ollama locally)
- **Concurrency**: `asyncio`
- **Data Modeling / Validation**: `pydantic`

---

## 📄 README Maintenance Guardrail

`README.md` is the **primary human-facing entry point** for this project: a short,
high-level front door aimed at both users and developers. Detailed material lives
in `docs/` and is linked from the README. The agent MUST keep both current at all
times.

### When to update

Update the relevant file whenever any of the following change:

| Change type | Where to update |
|---|---|
| New or removed Python file / package | `README.md` **Code Overview** |
| New dependency added (`pip install ...`) | `README.md` **Quick Start → Prerequisites** |
| New way to run the project | `README.md` **Quick Start** and `docs/living-studio.md` |
| New MCP tool or capability | `README.md` **Code Overview** / relevant doc |
| New CLI command or flag | `docs/cli.md` |
| New connector kind | `docs/connectors.md` |
| New workflow or agent instruction | `docs/living-studio.md` |
| Deployment URL or cloud setup changes | `docs/deployment.md` |
| Roadmap item completed or added | `docs/roadmap.md` |
| Test layout or coverage changes | `docs/development.md` |

### Rules

- ✅ **Update docs in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
- ✅ **Keep README short**: it stays a high-level orientation page. Push detail into `docs/` and link to it rather than growing the README.
- ✅ **Keep the Quick Start accurate**: always reflect `uv run python scripts/dev.py` as the recommended launch command.
- ✅ **Keep Prerequisites up to date**: add any new `pip install` dependency immediately.
- ✅ **Mark Roadmap items `[x]` when completed** — do not leave stale unchecked items.
- ❌ **Never leave the README or `docs/` in a stale state** where documented commands or files no longer match the codebase.

---

## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails

### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
- **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
- **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
  - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
  - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
- **Tool Creation**: 
  - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
  - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
  - **Contract Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` (`ToolName`, `TOOL_SPECS`) and the `get_capabilities` return string. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` enforces the surface.

### 2. Async / Client Practices
- Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
- Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.

### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
- Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
- When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.

### 4. General Philosophy
- **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
- **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
- **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `packages/connectors` workspace package. New kinds implement `agentic_odi_connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
- **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.

### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
- **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
- **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
- **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `packages/connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
- **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
- **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
- **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
- **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Proves the Living Studio updater end to end against a local release feed:
#
#   1. generates a throwaway minisign key
#   2. builds signed 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 AppImages pointed at a local latest.json
#   3. runs 0.1.0 and waits for it to install 0.2.0 over its own file
#   4. runs the result again and asserts it checks, finds nothing, and downloads
#      nothing
#
# This is a manual proof, not part of CI: it builds the desktop shell twice and
# needs a Linux display plus AppImage/FUSE support. Run it from a workstation:
#
#   bash scripts/verify-desktop-update.sh
#
# The throwaway key means the built AppImages only trust this test feed; the
# committed public key is untouched.
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
STUDIO="$REPO_ROOT/apps/studio"
WORK="${WORK:-/tmp/studio-update-e2e}"
PORT="${PORT:-8787}"
OLD_VERSION="0.1.0"
NEW_VERSION="0.2.0"

APP_PID=""
SERVER_PID=""

cleanup() {
  if [ -n "$APP_PID" ] && kill -0 "$APP_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill "$APP_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$APP_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  if [ -n "$SERVER_PID" ] && kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

say() { printf '\n\033[1m==> %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }

rm -rf "$WORK"
mkdir -p "$WORK/feed" "$WORK/run"

parts.text:
So #70 and #64 truly have **NO GitHub Actions CI at the head commit** — only the Cloudflare Workers check (failing). Their earlier commits had CI runs, but the head commits (which contain the destructive snapshot) never triggered a CI run.

Why? The head commit for #70 is `4201bf69` — an EMPTY commit (no file changes). GitHub Actions has `paths-ignore`? No, ci.yml has no path filters. But GitHub Actions skips workflow runs when a push contains no file changes relative to the previous commit? No, that's not true for push events... Actually, GitHub Actions DOES skip a workflow run if the push contains only changes that are ignored by `paths`/`paths-ignore` filters. But with no filters it always runs.

Hmm — actually, GitHub Actions skips workflow dispatch and push events when the commit is "empty" in the sense of no diff? No.

Wait: for #70 the head is `4201bf69` (empty commit). The CI ran for `81f99a80` and `98dca3d0`. Let me check what commits are in the branch: 81f99a80, c5198e55, 9d462518, a0df40f1, 4201bf69. CI runs exist only for 81f99a80 and 98dca3d0 (the latter is maybe an earlier version). So the destructive commit c5198e55 and everything after never got CI.

Actually, more likely: the CI workflow run for the head was *superseded* — no. Or the runs were triggered but failed to start? Let me check `gh run list --branch` for the specific head SHA with all statuses.

Actually, I saw for #62: CI ran for `471a333e` (the head) and succeeded. For #66, let me check.

Let me look more carefully — the `gh pr checks` for #70/#64 shows only the Cloudflare check. This means GitHub has no check runs for the head SHA. Let me query the check-runs API for the head SHAs.

This is a meaningful CI signal: **#70 and #64 have no CI verification on their current head** — and their head contains the destructive snapshot commit.

Let me verify with the API.

# Open PR Audit — `alehar9320/agentic-odi`

## 0. Scope and completeness

`gh pr list --state open --limit 60` returns **exactly 7 open PRs** — your list was complete. No drafts, no PRs from forks, no hidden PRs. `gh issue list --state all` returns **1 issue** (#77 "Add buy-me-a-coffee", open, no labels, created 19:51).

**Headline finding: 6 of 7 open PRs are structurally poisoned.** They are Jules-generated branches that each contain one *tree-replacement* commit which overwrites the repo with a stale snapshot, silently reverting 4–5 recently merged features. They pass CI *because* the reverted tree is internally self-consistent. The one human-authored PR (#76) is the only healthy one.

---

## 1. Per-PR breakdown

### #76 — `feat(studio): make the desktop app update itself` — **REAL, high quality**

| | |
|---|---|
| Branch | `feat/studio-auto-update` (1 commit, `af849564`) |
| Base | `624b6857` = current `origin/main` HEAD. Behind by 0. |
| Diff | 37 files, +3431/−118 |
| CI | **All green** — `CI green`, lint, typecheck, security, test (3.10/3.11/3.12), smoke, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build, website, Cloudflare Workers Builds all `pass` |
| Mergeability | `MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN` |
| Reverts anything? | **No** — the only PR that deletes nothing from main |

**What it actually changes**

New module `apps/studio/src/updater/` (9 source + 4 test files):
- `types.ts` (107 L) — domain vocabulary
- `machine.ts` (306 L) — pure reducer `reduce(snapshot, event)` + selectors `progressPercent`, `bannerView`, `canRestartNow`, `describeCheckedAt`, `statusLine`
- `service.ts` (446 L) — schedule → check → download → install → relaunch, with injected transport/storage/clock
- `transport.ts` (61 L) — the only module importing Tauri plugins
- `platform.ts` (31 L) — `installAfterDownload()` returns `platform !== "windows"`
- `UpdateProvider.tsx` (58 L), `UpdateBanner.tsx` (120 L), `UpdateSettings.tsx` (105 L)

**78 dedicated tests**: `machine.test.ts` (34 `it()`), `service.test.ts` (24), `transport.test.ts` (7), `UpdateBanner.test.tsx` (6), `UpdateSettings.test.tsx` (7). It also *replaces* the old `apps/studio/src/components/updater/useUpdater.ts` (deleted) and rewires `SettingsPanel.tsx` — no dangling import.

**Release pipeline fixes (the actually-important part)**
- `release-please-config.json:5-22` — adds `extra-files` for `apps/studio/package.json`, `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, `apps/studio/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`. Without this the installed version can never move. Note `tauri.conf.json:6` is still `"version": "0.1.0"` on main — this is the smoking gun the PR fixes (now `0.12.0`).
- `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml:6-9` and `.github/workflows/release.yml:6-8` — add `release: types: [published]` because release-please publishes via API and never emits `push: tags`.
- `tauri-release.yml:129-168` — new `verify` job that fails the release if `latest.json` is absent, advertises the wrong version, or lacks signed artifacts for `linux-x86_64`, `windows-x86_64`, `darwin-aarch64`, `darwin-x86_64`.
- `scripts/verify-desktop-update.sh` (189 L) — real E2E: throwaway minisign key, two signed AppImages, local `latest.json`, watches 0.1.0 replace its own file.

**Security surface**: `apps/studio/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json:6` adds `process:default`; `src-tauri/src/lib.rs:61-63` registers `tauri_plugin_process::init()` for the in-place relaunch. Minimal and justified.

**What is left un-done**
1. No PR publishes a release — the first release after merge is the first with a working `latest.json`. Body acknowledges this.

## 5. Repo CI / release / branch-protection state, and churn

### Branch protection
- `GET /branches/main/protection` → **404 "Branch not protected"**. There is no classic branch protection.
- There **is** a ruleset: `id 25356329`, name **`main-requires-ci-green`**, created 2026-10-18, `enforcement: active`, requiring status check **`CI green`** on the default branch.
- `bypass_actors: [{actor_id: 5, actor_type: RepositoryRole, bypass_mode: "always"}]` — **role 5 = admin, i.e. the repo owner, can merge to `main` with the check unsatisfied, with no warning.**
- `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false` — a branch that has never run CI can satisfy the check.

**The critical implication: #70 and #64 have NO `CI green` run on their head SHA and an aggregate commit status of `pending`.** They are blocked by the ruleset *only because the owner has not used the admin bypass*. #66, #65, #63, #62 all have green `CI green` and are `MERGEABLE` — one click from silently reverting 9–11 merged features.

### CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
Jobs: `lint` (ruff check + format), `typecheck` (mypy apps packages; mypy website), `security` (bandit on apps/packages/website), `test` (pytest ×3.10/3.11/3.12 with coverage), `smoke`, `website`, `studio` (npm lint/typecheck/test/build **+ a `gen:api-types` drift check**), `tauri-check` (fmt/clippy/check), `tauri-build` (unsigned-or-signed bundle), and an aggregator `ci-green` that fails unless every job succeeded.

Two things to note:
- The `studio` job's **`Verify generated API types are up to date`** step is the only structural guard against schema drift, and it is exactly the guard that #70 and #62 both trip (both regenerate `openapi.json` + `schema.d.ts`).
- There is **no `paths`/`paths-ignore` filter**, so CI should run on every push. The fact that the destructive commits (`c5198e55`, `76192e1b`) and their successors never produced a run is unexplained by the workflow config and worth investigating — the timeline shows runs at 20:40–21:04 for #62/#63/#65/#66 but a gap for #70 and #64 entirely after 19:41.

### Release flow
- `release-please-config.json`: `release-type: simple`, single package `.`. **No `extra-files`** → the Tauri app's version is not bumped by release-please. #76 fixes this.
- `.release-please-manifest.json`: `"0.12.0"`. Releases observed: 0.7.0 → 0.8.0 → 0.9.0 → 0.10.0 → 0.11.0 → 0.12.0 (PRs #30, #32, #52, #57, #67, #75) — **six release PRs in a single day**, all `+8…+22` lines, all hand-merged within minutes of each other.
- `release.yml` triggers on `push: tags: v*`; `tauri-release.yml` likewise. **Neither fired for any of the 6 releases** because release-please publishes via API and emits no tag-push event. So **no desktop bundle, no `latest.json`, and no signed updater artifacts have ever been published.** #76 fixes the trigger and adds a `verify` job that makes this loud.
- `allow_auto_merge: true`, `delete_branch_on_merge: false` → **~50 remote branches will accumulate** (already 50+ on `origin`).
- `has_wiki: true`, `has_issues: true`; `open_issues_count: 8` reported by the API but only **1** issue visible via `gh issue list` (the other 7 are open PRs).
